name: flat_normal
label: no_page
rationale: Steady latency with ordinary noise for the whole run. Nothing to act on.

name: noisy_normal_with_single_point_spikes
label: no_page
rationale: Higher variance and isolated single-sample spikes every 10 to 15 minutes, throughout. A noisy p99 at low traffic. No trend, no clustering.

name: single_spike_recovered
label: no_page
rationale: One 30 second spike to 5x at minute 82, normal before and after. A transient.

name: short_blip_recovered
label: no_page
rationale: Two minutes at up to 3x around minute 78, then back to normal. Review in the morning.

name: mild_drift_up
label: no_page
rationale: Latency drifts up about 15 percent between minute 60 and 150. Too small and too slow to page. A ticket at most.

name: step_down_improvement
label: no_page
rationale: A deploy at minute 90 cuts latency by a third and it stays there. A change, but an improvement.

name: periodic_small_bumps
label: no_page
rationale: A 30 second bump of 1.5x every 5 minutes, identical for the whole run. A cron job or GC cycle, not an incident.

name: low_traffic_jitter
label: no_page
rationale: Wide random jitter between roughly 0.6x and 2x with no structure. A percentile over very few requests at night.

name: rise_then_full_recovery
label: no_page
rationale: Latency climbs from 260 to about 420 ms over 14 minutes, peaks at minute 94, and is back to baseline by minute 108. A bump, never a problem.

name: deploy_warmup
label: no_page
rationale: At minute 100 latency jumps to 2.5x and decays back to normal within 3 minutes. Cold start after a rollout.

name: past_data_gap
label: no_page
rationale: Three minutes of missing data at minute 85, normal latency before and after. A scrape hiccup.

name: spike_cluster_recovered
label: no_page
rationale: Three spikes of 3x to 4x between minute 80 and 85, then clean baseline. Worth a look tomorrow.

name: stable_sawtooth
label: no_page
rationale: A sawtooth with a 10 minute period and constant 1.6x amplitude, repeating identically. Periodic cache refill.

name: mean_reverting_wander
label: no_page
rationale: Slow wandering within about plus or minus 20 percent, always returning to the middle.

name: one_minute_outage_recovered
label: no_page
rationale: One minute pinned at the timeout ceiling at minute 74, then completely normal. Over before anyone could react. This is what a for duration exists for.

name: step_up_sustained
label: page
rationale: Latency jumps 5x at minute 95 and stays there. Five minutes of a sustained 5x is enough to page.

name: ramp_still_climbing
label: page
rationale: From minute 90 latency climbs linearly from 200 ms, passing 1 s around minute 117 and reaching 2 s by the end. Page once it is clearly past 1 s and still climbing.

name: timeout_plateau
label: page
rationale: From minute 105 every sample sits at the 30 second timeout ceiling. Two minutes of that is enough.

name: exponential_blowup
label: page
rationale: Slow rise from minute 80 that keeps accelerating: 1.9x at minute 115, 3.4x at minute 130, 12x at the end. Page when the curve is clearly bending up.

name: flapping
label: page
rationale: From minute 100 latency alternates between normal and 8x every 5 minutes. After the second flap it is clearly unstable.

name: post_deploy_regression
label: page
rationale: A step from 200 ms to 1.2 s at minute 75 that never comes back. Five to fifteen minutes in, it needs a rollback.

name: steady_degradation
label: page
rationale: Monotonic climb from 220 ms at minute 60 to about 2.2 s at minute 150, no plateau. Passes 1 s around minute 95. Page once it is clearly past the point of being a nuisance.

name: growing_spikes
label: page
rationale: From minute 68 a spike every 6 minutes, each taller and longer than the last: 2x at first, 6.5x by minute 98, over 10x later. Page once the escalation is clear.

name: step_to_1200ms_sustained
label: page
rationale: A step from 300 ms to 1.2 s at minute 80, sustained for the rest of the run. Ten minutes of that breaches any reasonable SLO.

name: sawtooth_growing_amplitude
label: page
rationale: A normal sawtooth between 250 and 380 ms whose peaks start growing after minute 60: 600 ms, 830 ms, 1.05 s, 1.3 s and on. Each cycle ends worse than the last.

name: spike_then_sustained_break
label: page
rationale: A one minute 6x spike at minute 80 that fully recovers, then a 5x jump at minute 110 that holds until the end. The first one is noise, the second one is the page.

name: bimodal_half_fleet
label: page
rationale: From minute 100 samples alternate between normal and 10x. Half the requests are fine and half are not: one bad instance behind the balancer.

name: two_min_spike_recovered
label: no_page
rationale: Two minutes at 1.7 s from minute 100, then back to 210 ms for good. Big but short, over before a for duration would expire.

name: slow_ramp_to_340ms
label: no_page
rationale: A smooth climb from 190 to 340 ms between minute 60 and 150. Abnormal, not harmful. A morning ticket, not a page.

name: two_stage_degradation
label: page
rationale: A step from 230 to 460 ms at minute 85, then a second step to 1.4 s at minute 110, both sustained. The first stage is a ticket, the second is a page.

name: low_traffic_sparse_slow_requests
label: no_page
rationale: Night traffic: a few requests per 15 s bucket, so p99 is the single slowest request. One sample in four lands between 1 and 1.5 s all night long, never two in a row, while the typical value stays at 180 ms. Nothing changed and nobody is affected.
